title: Lower Bounds for all List-Decodable Deletion Codes
summary: A length-$n$ binary $k$-deletion code is a set of binary strings such that if we delete any $k$ bits of a string, leaving a length-$(n-k)$ binary string, we can uniquely recover the codeword. In this paper, we consider $t$-list decodable deletion codes, where after $k$ bits of a codeword are deleted, we can identify a list of size at most $t$ such that the original codeword lies in the list.
